fixes.explanation: Not this time, friend. A long life never comes up in this psalm. His first words are “O LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger or discipline me in Your wrath.” That's the first thing out of his mouth.
That's right. David says, “My beloved and friends shun my disease, and my kinsmen stand at a distance.” The people closest to him keep their distance. I think that would sting on top of the pain.
Iniquity, yes. David says, “Yes, I confess my iniquity; I am troubled by my sin.” He doesn't dodge or dress it up. That's a hard thing to do, friend.

Loyalty isn't the word, friend. The verse says, “Yes, I confess my iniquity; I am troubled by my sin.” Iniquity means wrongdoing, and that's what David owns up to. I'd say that's a big step, and no loyalty card gets him out of it.
That's it. David prays, “Do not forsake me, O LORD; be not far from me, O my God.” After all that groaning, he asks the LORD to stay close. I think that tells us a lot, friend.

He doesn't ask for that here, friend. David prays, “Do not forsake me, O LORD; be not far from me, O my God.” Strength isn't in that request. He asks the LORD not to leave him and not to be far away, and I think that's a prayer worth copying.
